name: Fixed jackets and gravity-based structures
applications: shallow to mid-depth fields, including Malaysia and the North Sea
principle: Fixed platforms stand on steel jackets piled to the seabed or on concrete gravity-based structures (GBS) that can store oil; they are economic to about 520 m of water. Bullwinkle (Gulf of Mexico) is the tallest fixed example at 529 m, and Hibernia's GBS weighs about 1.2 million tons with 1.3 million barrels of storage.

process_steps.name: Float out, install and pile or ballast

notes: Process provenance: Documents jacket and GBS concepts with execution phases - jacket pile arrangements (through-leg, skirt, vertical skirt), fabrication on the quay, load-out and sea-fastening, lift-and-upend or launch installation, piling and topsides installation; for GBS, concrete base fabrication, barge positioning between columns, deballasting to receive the deck, tow-out and set-down by ballasting.
